name: Pyramids of Giza
desc: 4,500 years old and still the flex. Stand where pharaohs planned forever and feel your rent worries shrink to sand.

name: Grand Egyptian Museum
desc: Tut's gold under one colossal new roof. Save up, walk in broke, walk out feeling like a king's accountant.

name: Egyptian Museum (Tahrir)
desc: The dusty-pink OG on Tahrir — mummies, sarcophagi, and a century of gloriously packed halls.

name: Khan el-Khalili
desc: Lantern-lit maze of brass, spice, and haggling since the 1300s. Browsing is free; mint tea is basically mandatory.

name: Al-Azhar Park
desc: A green hill over old Cairo for the price of a candy bar. Sunset plus a thousand minarets — cheapest cinema in town.

name: Citadel of Saladin
desc: A hilltop fortress with an alabaster mosque and a skyline that runs all the way to the pyramids on a clear day.

name: Cairo Tower
desc: Lotus-shaped 60s tower over the Nile. Go at night and count the city lights you can't afford yet.

name: Nile Corniche
desc: The riverside stroll every Cairene knows. Feluccas drift by, tea vendors appear, and nobody charges you for the moon.

name: Al-Muizz Street
desc: A kilometer of Fatimid Cairo lit up like an open-air museum after dark. Free time travel, batteries not required.

name: Coptic Cairo
desc: The Hanging Church, hushed lanes, and two thousand years stacked in layers — all before lunch.
